definitions.explanation: A humorous remark, story, or prank intended to make people laugh. In Japanese, ジョーク tends to imply a more Western-style verbal joke, as opposed to Japanese-style humor.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ジョーク⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{皆|みんな}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{笑|わら}った→笑う：00685_warau⟧。
ジョーク⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦つもり→つもり：01152_tsumori⟧だった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{怒|おこ}らせて→怒る：00876_okoru⟧しまった。
examples.english: I meant it as a joke, but I ended up making the other person angry.

notes:
USAGE:
ジョーク implies a verbal joke or witty remark. Related terms include ⟦{冗談|じょうだん}→冗談：03347_joudan⟧ (joke, kidding — more commonly used in daily conversation), ⟦ユーモア→ユーモア：00432_yuumoa⟧ (humor), and ⟦ギャグ→ギャグ：10810_gyagu⟧ (gag — physical or slapstick comedy).

ジョーク⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦つもり→つもり：01152_tsumori⟧ means "intended as a joke" and is commonly used when humor is misunderstood.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ジョーク⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧: to tell a joke
- ジョーク⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飛|と}ばす→飛ばす：02373_tobasu⟧: to crack jokes
- ブラックジョーク: dark joke, black humor
- ジョーク⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{通|つう}じない→通じる：02289_tsuujiru⟧: the joke doesn't get through (not understood)
